title: Lulu’s Law
summary: This bill orders the Federal Communications Commission to formally allow shark attacks to be sent out as wireless emergency alerts — the alert system defined in the FCC's existing rules (47 CFR 10.10(a)). The FCC has 180 days after the bill becomes law to issue the order.
brief: Requires the FCC to issue an order making a shark attack an event for which a wireless emergency alert may be transmitted.

top_lines.headline: Shark Attack Alerts
subs: FCC must allow shark attacks to qualify for wireless emergency alerts
Uses the existing 'Alert Message' system defined in FCC rules (47 CFR 10.10(a))

top_lines.headline: FCC Deadline
subs: FCC has 180 days after enactment to issue the order

likelihoodReason: Signed into law on June 26, 2026. Sponsored by Sen. Katie Britt (R-AL) with 9 cosponsors from both parties; the narrow directive adding a hazard category to an existing alert system cleared both chambers (Senate by unanimous consent, House 401-6) before being signed.

items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Directs the FCC to issue an order providing that a shark attack is an event for which an Alert Message may be transmitted, no later than 180 days after enactment.
items.detail: The bill ties the term 'Alert Message' to the definition in section 10.10(a) of title 47 of the Code of Federal Regulations (or any successor regulation), so it works within the FCC's existing Wireless Emergency Alerts framework rather than creating a new alert type. The bill specifies only that the order be issued within the 180-day window; it sets no further conditions on how the alerts are triggered or administered.

gaps: The bill makes shark attacks eligible for wireless emergency alerts but does not specify which authorities may originate such an alert or what criteria define a qualifying shark attack.
The bill sets a 180-day deadline for the FCC order but specifies no consequence or backstop if the order is not issued on time.
The bill addresses only that an alert may be transmitted, but does not address the geographic area, duration, or content standards for a shark-attack alert.

added: An FCC order designating a shark attack as an event eligible for a wireless emergency Alert Message, to be issued within 180 days of enactment

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass
